The General Assembly has demonstrated since 2025 its leadership and several times as a lodestar for law, solidarity with victims, sovereign equality of states and defense of the foundations of the international order and of the Charter. It acted as such a lodestar on the 12th of September when it endorsed the New York Declaration on the peaceful settlement of the question of Palestine and the implementation of the two-state solution, which was the outcome of the international conference it had itself decided to convene as part of its 10th emergency special session. It was also such a lodestar when it reaffirmed twice on the 24th of February 2025 its support for a comprehensive, just and lasting peace in Ukraine in accordance with the principles of the Charter. These were its seventh and eighth resolutions since the outbreak of Russia's war of aggression in 2022. Mr. President, France advocates an open and effective multilateralism that represents us in all of our diversity. Linguistic diversity is at the forefront of diversities. Multilingualism is a fundamental value of the United Nations and contributes to the legitimacy, inclusiveness, and effectiveness of decision making within our organization. Its effective implementation on a daily basis remains a challenge, and it must not become an adjustment variable in ongoing budgetary efforts. Geographical diversity and gender equality are also of particular importance, and this is highlighted in resolution 79/327. France is committed to these principles in accordance with the Charter regarding the selection of senior UN officials, including the Secretary-General. The General Assembly plays an important role in the selection process, which was modernized in 2015 and reaffirmed this year. In this regard, We reiterate our call to Member States to submit female candidates. Mr. President, in conclusion, please be assured of France's full commitment to continue with its engagement in the process of revitalizing the work of the General Assembly. I thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of France. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Morocco.

Mr. President, the Kingdom of Morocco is very pleased to take part in this joint debate devoted to two essential dimensions of the functioning of our organization, namely the implementation of United Nations resolutions and the revitalization of the work of the General Assembly, which respectively give effect to our decisions and effectively guide our multilateral action. My delegation emphasizes that the effective implementation of resolutions adopted by General Assembly must remain based on transparency, respect for intergovernmentality and accountability. It's important to have a coherent, consistent implementation to preserve Member States' trust in the multilateral system and to ensure continuity in the normative operational work of the UN. The Kingdom also attaches great importance to better coordination amongst the principal organs of the United Nations. This enhanced coordination is indispensable to ensure consistency of mandates and to guarantee an integrated approach to the three pillars of the UN, whilst respecting the prerogatives of each organ. Mr. President, on the issue of revitalizing the General Assembly, here, Morocco welcomes the progress achieved under Resolution 79/327. which strengthens ongoing efforts to modernize and streamline the work of our Assembly. In this regard, my delegation wishes to highlight three elements. First, the need to rationalize the work program, make the organization of debates more structured, and improve resource utilization. Second, the strengthening of transparency and predictability of the calendar, so as to improve the participation of all member states. and thirdly, the enhancement of the role of the President of the General Assembly, including as a facilitator of consensus-building processes. Furthermore, Morocco is following with interest the UN80 initiative, which aims to improve system coherence, optimize the life cycle of mandates, and strengthen the operational capacity of intergovernmental bodies. This initiative must remain fully Member State driven and be based on regular and inclusive consultations. Mr. President, to conclude, please allow me to say that we remain convinced that the rigorous implementation of resolutions and the effective revitalization of the General Assembly constitute the foundation of a more effective, more representative, and results-oriented multilateralism. The Kingdom will continue its constructive engagement to contribute to a United Nations that is more modern, more transparent, and better adapted to the multiple, successive, and multidimensional challenges of our time. I thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of Morocco. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of the Russian Federation.

Mr. President, we welcome the convening of the General Assembly plenary meeting on the issue of UN resolution implementations and the revitalization of the Assembly's work. The Russian Federation actively participates in advancing the revitalization agenda of the General Assembly, which is aimed at strengthening the authority and effectiveness of this organ. This task is becoming particularly important important in light of growing geopolitical tensions and new global challenges and threats. Given the latest liquidity crisis at the UN, what has become exposed are many shortcomings in the functioning of its system, including inflated mandates, the overfilling the field presence with non-core tasks, and donors' obsessive promotion of their own priorities, which remain alien and irrelevant to the needs of recipient countries. The key to optimizing the work of the General Assembly lies in further refining its working methods and streamlining its agenda, which remains overloaded. It remains relevant to shift some agenda items on the GA agenda to a biennial, triennial basis and removing outdated ones. This process must be approached in a well-considered way. This session will focus on implementing resolution 79327 on revitalization, which resulted from a fragile compromise reached during the previous session of the GA. We expect that the co-chairs of the working group will be able to conduct all planned discussions, organize a thorough and impartial review of existing weaknesses in organizing the work of bodies, and also find ways to reduce the politicization of debates. The revitalization process should not mean reallocating powers to the General Assembly, the powers that belong to other bodies under the UN, including the Security Council. We, therefore, have consistently been insisting on strict compliance with the Charter provisions regarding the Security Council's primary responsibility for maintaining international peace and security. Mr. President, During this session, substantial work lies ahead in selecting candidates for the next UN Secretary-General. We expect that very soon the letter from the Presidents of the General Assembly and Security Council, President launching this process, will be agreed very soon. As President of the Security Council in October, the Russian Federation started work on drafting this document, responding to numerous calls from Member States for a timely start to this process. We expect that the President of the General Assembly will approach her task in this area very responsibly, and this will be done based on Article 97 of the UN Charter and will promote the constructive development of this process, given its very special importance and sensitivity. We must not forget that the main goal here is to elect the most merit-worthy candidate. We also expect that the President of the General Assembly throughout the session will closely adhere to the Code of Ethics, which requires her to maintain high standards of neutrality, impartiality, and equidistance. The issue of implementing General Assembly resolutions remain extremely important for us. It is regrettable that some states try to apply double standards when considering resolutions on various issues. And whenever the content of those does not align with their interests, they seek to block them using various pretexts. We proceed on the basis that most decisions in this hall aimed at improving diverse aspects of human life must and will be implemented because this is in our common interest. Russia confirms its readiness to work constructively in this area under the leadership of the co-chairs of the Working Group on Strengthening and Revitalizing the General Assembly. I thank you for your attention.
I thank the distinguished representative of the Russian Federation. by now, give the floor to the distinguished representative of Brazil.

Mr. President, Brazil is proud to have actively participated in the negotiations leading to the adoption of resolution 79/327 on the revitalization of the works of the General Assembly. In this regard, we regret that the ongoing liquidity crisis is negatively impacting deliberations of the Assembly and its committees, especially the Third Committee, where the general debate on agenda items has been temporarily suspended, presumes of the view that this exceptional circumstance in no way constitutes a precedent to be followed. In addition, the legitimate objective of streamlining our work and avoiding the duplication of efforts must never be used for political purposes. No agenda item, debate, or dialogue can be eluded under the pretext of revitalizing the work of the Assembly. Mr. President, Brazil values the resolution's emphasis on the imperative to ensure gender balance and the equitable geographical representation in the process of selection and appointment of the next Secretary-General of the United Nations. The resolution strengthens our commitment to a transparent, inclusive, and predictable process in line with the UN Charter. We look forward to the official launching of the process in the upcoming weeks, as established in the resolution. Brazil also firmly believes that it's high time for the next Secretary-General to be a qualified woman from the Latin American and Caribbean region. We have many talented and experienced names to offer to the United Nations. Brazil remains fully engaged and committed to ensuring that this process is fair, transparent, and truly representative of the diversity of our organization. Thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of Brazil. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Timor-Leste.

Mr. President, the Maltese Alliance follows the statement delivered by Malaysia on behalf of ASEAN and Algeria on behalf of NAM. As a proud member state of the United Nations, we reaffirm our commitment to multilateral cooperation, to human dignity, to global solidarity, and to ensuring the that one voice, one country truly matters in this Assembly. We extend our sincere appreciation to all those who, over the past year, who have worked tirelessly to strengthen this institution, giving renewed relevance to the Assembly, especially in a moment when the world is rocked by overlapping crises, increasing inequality, climate disruptions, and geopolitical fragmentation. Particularly, we welcome the adoptions of resolutions 79/327, which some describe as linking revitalization with wider UN reform efforts, including the UN Act initiative and the Pact for the Future. The action is aligned with our collective resolve to renew the General Assembly's relevance to make this body not only equal for all Member States, but practically effective for all peoples. From the experience of Timor-Leste, which has drawn on conflict and recovery to achieve peace building and institutions building, as well as today's effort to diversify our economy, create jobs, and improve health and education, we know that global aspiration must translate into national realities. A stronger, more coherent General Assembly can make exactly that difference. The global future remains sovereign. According to UN Sustainable Development Goals Report, 2025, only about 17% of SDG targets worldwide are on track, and lower and middle income countries face mounting financial shortfalls. Debt servicing in these countries reach a record 1.4 trillion U.S. in 2024, funds that might otherwise have been allocated to poverty reductions, education, climate action, and health. These figures underscore the urgency of today's topic, revitalization. The Assembly is not cosmetic, it is essential. Mr. President, Timor-Leste Our UN Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework 2021-2025 and our national SDG roadmap clearly show progress, but there are also remaining gaps. However, we cannot ignore the fact that for many countries, the gap between ambition and means remain wide. Strengthening the General Assembly about more than institutional reform. It is about providing more equitable support, predictable financing, stronger coordination, and meaningful representations for those often squeezed between ambition, goals, and resources constraints. Timor-Leste support the revitalization agenda, which addressing core areas where the General Assembly must involve, including First, enhancing coordination across UN bodies to avoid duplication, improve clarity, and reduce fragmentation, including stronger links with the United Nations Security Council and the United Nations Economic and Social Council. Second, streamlining agenda items, consolidating documentation, promoting informal, interactive debates, and thematic discussions, and engage all member states. not as passive observers, but as active participants. Third, strengthen the Assembly's role in peace and security, particularly when the Security Council is unable to act decisively via mechanisms such as the Uniting for Peace resolutions or Link Initiative. Mr. President, ultimately, we view the revitalized General Assembly as a bridge A bridge between global norms and local realities, between promise and delivery, a forum where small states and developing countries can not only speak, but be heard, where our experience matters, where outcomes translate into opportunities for our people. In conclusion, Mr. President, Timor-Leste stands ready to engage actively with all Member States in implementing this reform agenda. Drawing on our experience in peacebuilding, institution building, and SDG implementation, we believe that a more agile, inclusive, effective General Assembly will accelerate our collective progress toward a just, sustainable, and peaceful world. I thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of Timor-Leste. And I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of United Arab Emirates.

Mr. President, at the outset, the United Arab Emirates aligns itself with the statement delivered on behalf of the Non-Aligned Movement. We thank the co-chairs of the ad hoc working group on revitalization in the 79th session for their valuable stewardship towards the adoption of resolution 79327 by consensus. Mr. President, as we prepare for another session of engagement on this important topic, and as we consider the UN80 initiative for a more efficient and effective UN, allow me to highlight three main points. First, the relationship between the General Assembly and the Security Council should be further strengthened, including in matters of international peace and security. Several developments deserve to be retained and built upon. These include the veto initiative established by resolution 76262, the annual plenary debate on the use of the veto, as well as the January meeting for member states and observers to present views on the Security Council's annual report. Equally important is the selection process of the Secretary-General, which brings me to my second point. As we approach the first stage of this process, before the end of the year, the two organs should continue to work in accordance with the UN Charter, relevant General Assembly resolutions and the post-2015 transparent and inclusive practice. Looking ahead, we encourage the General Assembly to articulate the leadership profile and competencies it seeks in the next Secretary-General. This role demands vision, integrity and impartiality. And as our challenges compound, the next Secretary-General will need to affirm the UN's role in conflict prevention and resolution, and uphold the Organization's principles and purposes. This must be complemented by the Secretary-General's leadership team, which will be critical in her or his success. Equal and fair distribution of the executive heads in terms of merit as well as gender and geographic balance would bolster the Secretary-General's efforts. I also underscore that our commitment to inclusivity and increasing female representation across the UN system includes electing the UN's first Madam Secretary-General. Third, the UAE reaffirms the continued importance of multilingualism as a core value of the UN. In particular, we emphasize the importance of issuing all documents on time in all official languages, including Arabic. Mr. President, the UAE continues to see relevance of further discussions to revitalize the General Assembly. including through efforts in the main committees as well as the General Committee, and we will remain engaged to this end. Thank you, Mr. President.

I thank the distinguished representative of the United Arab Emirates. We have heard now the last speaker in the debate on these items. The Assembly has thus concluded this stage of its consideration of agenda items 120 and 121. The meeting is adjourned.
